_what_this_is: THE RATCHET. Protected, so only a human commit can move these numbers. harness/ratchet.py asserts observed >= floor against the gate log after every full run, and with --base asserts floor(head) >= floor(base) - so 'delete the assertion and lower the number in the same commit' is not available. Until 2026-09-04 nothing read this file; the ratchet script is what made the previous sentence true.
_slack_is_zero_here_on_purpose: These are set EQUAL to what the harness currently observes, not below it. The gap between observed and floor is exactly the number of assertions that can be deleted with the gate still green, and it GROWS as the harness improves, because raising the floor is a protected edit the factory cannot make. Zero slack forces the raise into the same human commit that accepts the new assertions, which is mildly annoying every time and is the entire reason the number means something.
_where_each_count_comes_from: Every count is a marker ci.py prints and ratchet.py parses, and the ratchet is now rung 6 of a full run rather than a separate command the validation workflow remembered to call. static_checks is read from the STATIC_OK line, with harness/.run/static-checks kept as a fallback; contract_events, contract_fields and phrases_cases come from the static rung's own marker lines, which ci.py now lifts into the gate log.
_known_gap: The iOS app is outside the ratchet entirely: no floor can count a check that cannot run on these machines. harness/static_ios.py counts manifest checks and brace balance, and that count is inside static_checks; a compile is not (.factory/decisions.md D-005).
_raise_these: On the same human commit that adds the assertions. If you find yourself lowering one, the question is what stopped being true.
